newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU countryside at a cross roads, Fischler says.
newsitem.headline: EU countryside at a cross roads, Fischler says.

text.p: The European Union's agriculture policy has overshadowed its rural policy and there must be a new balance in the 21st century, EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Monday.

A conference organised by the Commission at Cork, Ireland, beginning on Thursday will be the turning point for rural areas which have tended to be viewed from an agricultural point of view in the past, he said.
"If the countryside is left to die then, progressively, the cities too will die out," he said.
He said that a dual policy combining agricultural interests and general rural interests will be needed in the future.
Saying that rural areas cover 80 percent of the EU and contain a quarter of the population he said:
"The time has come to start talking about policy for the 21st century. We have decided that rural areas will be affected and will need some impetus," he told the news conference.

The EU needs to build on the existing strengths of its diverse rural areas, The cultural identities of different areas should not be lost and jobs need to be created in sectors other than agriculture, he said.
He noted that the commisisoner for agriculture is also the commissioner for rural development.
"Previously we have had a policy where the CAP (Common Agricultural Policy) was substituting for a rural development policy," he said.
This had pushed rural policy into the margins and he said the same mistake should not be made again.
"I do not think we should make the opposite mistake. We need both policies," he added.
